review_title: Amazon customer service has sunk to new lows
review_text: Amazon customer service has sunk to new depths.  It seems the general approach is to throw out random explanations, no matter how untrue,  and hope one of them sticks.  Writing to executives is not helpful, as they just throw your issue to some Executive Response team, manned by the same low competence.    My issue stems from a google play gift card order via Amazon for an important birthday.  Two days after the order was accepted, and on the day the gift card was due to be delivered, it was arbitrarily cancelled.    The following saga ensues as I repeatedly contact customer service with two simple questions:  Why was the order cancelled and who cancelled it-  Agent says it was damaged in transit .... it’s an electronic gift card -  Same agent says I cancelled the order .... this is not the case -  Same agent says they can’t track anything as the order is over 30 days old .... the order was placed 5 days earlier -  The supervisor can’t figure out what happened and promises a response within 48 hours .... no response was ever received -  I escalate to CS-escalation and am told “not our problem, talk to the marketplace vendor for a refund.” ... refund was not the issue -  I escalate up the executive chain and i receive a response saying the payment was rejected by my bank.   I proceed to demonstrate that payment was in fact taken but reimbursed two days later  ... so not a rejection from the bank -  A different agent agrees that it was not a payment rejection and promises a response by Aug 20 ... I receive a response Aug 22-  The response states “an error on our end processing this refund” ... refund was not the issue  In short, terrible customer service and executives who don’t care about your experience.   Amazon has grown too big and indolent to care about quality.  It will cost them as more customers previously loyal, such as I, shift their purchasing to other more competent avenues.

review_title: Amazon was great, but not a great value anymore
review_text: I started using Amazon back in the 1990s as a graduate student. I purchased my textbooks there as it was cheaper than the university bookstore and tax free. Fast forward to 2008 when Amazon asked me to try prime for free. I did. And didn't realize they charged me $79 for the membership. I decided to keep it because products were cheaper than at on-ground stores, no taxes and free shipping. Then in 2012 China clamped down on counterfeit producers and stopped them from selling product in China. In 2012 Amazon opened the door to these Chinese sellers and Amazon became flooded with a bunch of junk products. The price of prime kept rising, but I kept it because of Prime video and 2-day delivery. When I became sick I relied on Amazon more. Now Amazon is expensive. They have moved lots of shows to Freevee, which I don't watch because I don't do ad TV. And to add insult to injury this year, 2024, they started adding ads to Prime Video and demanding an extra $3/month to remove the ads, citing all of the other services they added to Prime. I don't use those other services, so it is bloatware to me. Stuff isn't being delivered in 2 days anymore. And there have been times when products were lost in their shipping facilities and not delivered. You call Amazon and they outsource their customer service overseas, these people have no way to contact the drivers. This is rubbish. The seller ALWAYS has contact with shipping! Paying extra for same-day delivery doesn't guarantee it will be delivered same-day. Amazon stopped packing cushioning in boxes so I've received items damaged. I've received spoiled food items. I was horrified to learn the tea I was drinking expired months before. Once they shipped me pet food meant to be sold in Mexico. So, even though you purchase from one seller they ship the product that is closer to your domicile, which might not be the same quality. Prices aren't cheaper than the on-ground store anymore, sometimes it is higher. Taxes are included too. So there is no value to having Amazon anymore. I even submitted my SSN & 1099 to sell t-shirts on Amazon. They stopped adding people to the program that didn't have a huge social media following. But refused to delete my information from their database. Lastly, I purchased a product that was defective, a sports watch. I wanted to exchange it. The watch cost hundreds of dollars. The customer service rep wanted to offer me $25 for it. I demanded a supervisor and the US support team processed the exchange. When Hurricane Beryl was bearing down on Houston TX, I ordered the Midland NOAA radio bundle so I could be notified of tornados and floods should I lose power. My home was hit by a tornado in May 2024, so the threat was real. I paid extra for same day delivery. Amazon split the bundle with one part being delivered in a week and the other same-day, except they never delivered it and promised to deliver it AFTER the hurricane. I called and spoke to three reps. One had a fake barking dog sound and you couldn't hear a word she said. After 30 minutes she just told me to call the number I called to get her. Another promised to expedite it. He didn't. Finally I canceled the delivery with the third person. The product was sitting in Houston, I'm in Houston. I don't know why they refused to deliver it. I had to eventually purchase it from another company. This company that started out well is not the same as it was in the past when it cared about its customers. It doesn't care about its employees nor customers now, it only cares about profit. I will not be renewing my prime membership in October. And I will shop other online and on-ground retailers.

review_text: Once upon a time, in the magical land of Amazon.com, I embarked on a quest to buy a variety of items and even sell some of my own. Little did I know that this journey would be filled with both laughter and bewilderment.As a buyer, my experience has been mostly positive. Amazon's vast selection of products and speedy delivery make it a convenient choice for all your shopping needs. However, there have been times when I've encountered the occasional weirdness with returns. It's like trying to find a needle in a haystack while blindfolded and hopping on one foot.But fear not, dear reader, for I have discovered a hidden treasure! On rare occasions, I've managed to summon a human customer service representative. These elusive creatures are surprisingly pleasant and possess the power to make your problems disappear with a wave of their magical wand.Now, let's talk about the dark side of Amazon: the seller experience. As a small business owner, I must warn you that Amazon is a greedy and ridiculous platform. It's like a dragon hoarding all the gold and leaving you with just a few measly coins. Their policies are designed to maximize their own profits, leaving sellers feeling like they're on a never-ending quest for fairness.To all aspiring merchants out there, I would advise you to tread carefully in the treacherous realm of Amazon. Offer your products on their platform to reach a wider audience, but don't put all your eggs in this basket. Instead, create your own enchanted website and offer your wares at a slightly lower price. It's like offering a secret discount to those who dare to venture beyond the Amazon kingdom.In conclusion, dear reader, Amazon.com is a land of contrasts. As a consumer, you'll likely have a good experience, but as a seller, be prepared for a wild and unpredictable journey. So, gather your courage, sharpen your wit, and may the odds be ever in your favor!

review_title: I purchased a dive watch from Amazon on…
review_text: I purchased a dive watch from Amazon on 8/29/23. The item came on time. However, it was defective. So, rather than get a refund, I ordered a replacement on 9/2/23. The package was supposed to arrive in two to three days. I am still waiting for the item. It is now almost 9/18. I am a Prime customer, and have spent quite a lot of money with them over the years. I've called their customer service numerous times. I keep getting the same scripted answers. Sounds like a run-around to me. The item is in transit, they keep repeating. When I checked the USPS tracking history, the last date is 14 days ago, on 9/4/23, stating awaiting receipt of item. In other words, the Post Office hasn't even received the package. Even Amazon's own website says the package may be lost, and to request a refund or replacement. I was told to call back on 9/20 for them to investigate further. That's 18 days since I ordered the item. What a joke. I barely can understand these reps over the phone. Sound familiar? This is the last time I will ever order a big-ticket item from them. Before, Amazon promptly refunded me or sent out a replacement right away. This is how you lose loyal customers!Post Script (9/26/23): I was finally issued a refund,18 days after I purchased the watch. The item never arrived, nor did the USPS ever receive my package. I got an email from their customer service saying that the package was deemed 'not deliverable' and sent back to an Amazon facility. Just what I was telling them all along. As a Prime customer, I should not have to wait nearly three weeks. Amazon could have sent me a replacement. Again, this is not a good way to treat their loyal customers.

In recent times, there have been numerous instances of account closures by e-commerce giant Amazon without any explanation or proper communication to the affected customers. These abrupt closures have left customers frustrated, confused, and feeling violated. A negative trend of unexplained account closures is observed, highlighting the negative impact on customers and questioning the ethical practices of a company that prides itself on customer-centricity. Many customers, like myself, have fallen victim to Amazon's sudden account closures. Without warning or prior notice, access to accounts that have been faithfully used for years is abruptly terminated. When attempting to log in, a message appears stating that the account has been closed, with an email notification supposedly sent. However, in numerous cases, customers claim to have never received any such email or any details on how to resolve the situation.Adding to the frustration, attempts to seek clarification from Amazon's customer support often go unanswered. It is only when customers create new accounts and reach out to support that they receive a response, albeit in a rude form. The response typically states that the account was closed for violating the terms of the Conditions of Use agreement. However, customers vehemently deny any wrongdoing and are left perplexed by the lack of specific reasons for their account closures.Account closures without proper explanation or justification raise severe concerns about customer rights. As loyal patrons who have spent years and significant amounts of money on the platform, customers have the right to transparency and fair treatment. The sudden termination of access to accounts, which may contain valuable digital assets such as e-books and audio files, feels like a betrayal of trust. The alarming trend of unexplained account closures by Amazon raises serious questions about the company's commitment to customer satisfaction and respect for customer rights.

The second and even worse thing is sellers will start selling a good product and once it gets good reviews or if they can no longer get that product or whatever they will simply delete the photos, title, and description of the original product and then replace it with a new product that is often in the same category or related to the original product but far worse quality and almost never even interchangeable with the original (for example they replace a belt sander with a palm sander or drill or just different size brand and quality belt sander) and all they did was change the title, description and photos but kept the same listing since all they technically did was “edit it” which also allows them to keep all the positive reviews so you will be buying a product that is rated 5 stars and had hundreds of reviews and thus probably won’t even question it but yet you may be the first person to ever buy it because in essence they’re all fake reviews since they’re for the other product. The only way to tell is by reading the reviews and even then unless it has dozens of reviews or reviews with pictures of the product you’ll never know. Not only is that scummy and definitely worthy of a class action it could also really cause severe harm to people physically and monetarily because a lot of people get a lot of tips and info on the use, maintenance, parts, and accessories of products from the reviews especially on Chinese products that have useless instructions. It now transpires that on a large number of items Amazon has recently instigated a $7.99 pick up fee when requesting a pick up via UPS, or you can drive to the local drop off point which for me would cost around $12 in gas. This happened to me recently on items that arrive inoperable or damaged and despite assurances from a customer service person that it does not apply to faulty items I am still being charged!You will also notice a huge increase in sponsored items as you search Amazon. It used to be infrequently you would see a few sponsored items on a page but now some pages have more than 50% . Amazon seems to have found another way to make Jeff even more $$.Fake reviews have always been an issue recently commanding the attention of news outlets like CNN. In Amazons efforts to curtail these paid for reviews they are now blocking or banning genuine reviews. When they block a review you get a message that states: Amazon is not accepting reviews for this item from this e-mail address... review_title: SEEMS LIKE AMAZON FINANCIAL ENTRAPMENT TO ME
review_text: I received the wrong item from an Amazon purchase and returned it.  The total cost of the item was approx. $500.   I have returned purchases to Amazon many times and the returned funds have always posted against my Amazon credit card balance.  This time the credit posted to a non-existent Amazon gift card.  When returning the item, Amazon preselected “refund to your Amazon account balance”.  This in no way indicates it is returning the money to a non-existent gift card.  To add insult to injury purchases were posted against the gift card vs my Amazon credit card so they won’t refund the remaining gift card balance to my Amazon credit card!!  This seems to be entrapment, as Amazon’s messaging regarding where the funds are being returned to isn’t clear!  It seems Amazon is intentionally using vague language in their auto pre-selected option for returned funds to ensure customers spend the returned money through their company!  If this is unintentional, Amazon should add “gift card” to the auto pre-selected return funds option so customers understand the funds will not be returned to their Amazon credit card used to make the purchase, but instead be added to a non-existent gift card balance.  The gift card was created at the time of the refund!  As I stated above, this seems like financial entrapment to ensure returned funds remain with AMAZON vs being credited to the Amazon credit card used to make the purchase! I believe any reasonable person would assume “be returned to Amazon account balance” means being returned to your Amazon credit card balance.  Especially since at the time of the return there were no other Amazon account balances other than the credit card, there weren’t any gift cards on file, and every other refund processed through Amazon had been credited to my Amazon credit card balance. When “gift card” isn’t in the sentence of the pre-selected option, and Amazon has credit card options, it seems like it is an intentional action by Amazon to be vague in their messaging to entrap customer’s funds and ensure more funds are expended through Amazon!  I rarely write reviews, but felt people should know about Amazon’s ridiculous refund policy/messaging, as it could really cause harm to families already in financial distress due to the resent pandemic and resulting economic downturn.

I also tried their callback that said it was connected but I could hear nothing.I decided to make a complaint via their complaints email but then an email came back saying they’re no longer responding to these emails and sent me links to go back to all the methods I had previously tried via call back and chat which is a bot. I didn’t know if this was correct way but I was at a loss of what to do. I told them the problems I was having with Amazon, they said forget Amazon and told me to contact their customer services, gave me an email to take pictures of the damage and a telephone number to call. The seller had eased my stress about the return but still I wanted to speak to a human at Amazon so I continued for hours looking for a number. Then I found this number 0800 496 1081, which I found on gethuman.com, apparently you can speak to a human and yes you can. It wasn’t easy finding the number. My search for a human to speak to at Amazon seemed like mission impossible, which I think is actually what Amazon want. They don’t have it on their website and during my search for a number I found lots of people asking the same question. There must be a reason it’s hard to find and I can only think that’s what Amazon wants. Human’s cost money so it’s their way of making more profit but at the frustration and stress to the customer - hence the one star. I did speak to a human who was lovely but they sent me an email with a different 0800 contact number should I need to contact them regarding problems returning the TV via the seller. It’s a number I tried before getting the other 0800 number and you don’t get to speak to a human  you get a text that directs you to their website just to go around in circles. That 0800 number is useless, been there done that. So, everyone use the 0800 496 1081 to speak to an actual human. Once I find out how to make a complaint I shall post it on here because if we don’t tell Amazon our experiences how can they provide good customer service. This is their quote from an email sent from the human I spoke to ‘ Your feedback is helping us build Earth's Most Customer-Centric Company’. Got apologies and was told it should be to me in two days, if it wasn't to call them and they'd initiate a refund.It didn't show, and I called, and they issued a refund. Got a return authorization and label - but I got back with them and said I wasn't lugging it to UPS, that they should arrange a pickup, and they did with no problem.I think the issue with people's bad experience falls into two categories - not doing research on the items and the sellers, and the unfortunate choices Amazon makes about shipping. All my orders arrive either USPS or UPS.I do miss the two-day shipping, but I guess that's gone forever. So I have to plan ahead, and if it's urgent, all the stores are less than 20 minutes away.All that so say that in nearly two decades, I've never had any concerns about my Amazon purchases.

review_title: More incompetent at delivery than usual?
review_text: Due to a kidney transplant my vaccine probably doesn't protect me very well, and live alone, so at the moment (Aug 2021) I'm very dependent on delivery services.Amazon used to be fairly dependable.  Currently, they are anything but.  Over half of my recent deliveries have been delayed by 1-5 business days, with the occasional package simply being lost.  Whatever it is that's leading to the recent increase in incompetence, STOP LYING ABOUT THE DELIVERY DATE and provide a more accurate estimate that I can use for planning purposes.Also, the frequency with which packages are delivered to the wrong address is infuriating/appalling; on my account I provide detailed, clear directions on how to get to my door, yet about half of my deliveries are dropped off at the wrong building or doorstep in my apartment complex, and as someone who uses a cane to walk, I cannot go from door, up and down many flights of stairs, searching for my package, physically speaking.  Even more appallingly, on a few occasions, a driver has dropped all packages for the entire 6-building apartment complex outside in the open/rain in a big pile.  I've been on the phone a few dozen times with Amazon's customer shipping department over the past year about this exact same issue -- they look at my directions and remark on how clear and detailed they are, apologize, assure me that this will not happen again, but... it still does.  Might the issue be not to give each driver so many deliveries that they end up cutting corners and not bothering to look at the directions?It's a huge relief when I find out a package I ordered from Amazon is coming via UPS or FedEx because then I usually get it on time AND at the right location... and only needed to call each of those companies' customer service numbers once to fix the any misdelivery issues.

review_title: 2 Trips & A Lot of Hassle for a Razor
review_text: After a terrible customer service experience about 1.5 years ago, I stopped using Amazon. I’ve rented a couple of movies, but that’s it. My roommate constantly orders from them without much issue (excluding a book that took 3 months to get here), so I thought I’d try them again. Big big big big mistake. Firstly, I had updated my card info months ago; it’s the same one they charge when I rented movies. I place an $80 something order and a week goes by without an update. Mind you, I had also updated my contact info to TEXT me updates, rather than email, as I hardly ever check my email. Well, they tried to run the wrong card, and then sent me one email saying my order hadn’t processed. One would think before accepting an order, the business would first make sure it was paid for, but I guess that’s crazy talk. Anyway, I cancelled that order. I re-updated my payment info and placed another order of about the same price; I changed some things. One of the things I ordered was a new double bladed safety blade razor. I read the description REPEATEDLY and it said this particular razor, a Viking Chieftan, came with one blade. For me, that is what I needed; I’m not about to pay an extra $10 for 100 blades, if I don’t even know if I’ll like the product. I get the razor, and there isn’t a blade. I looked everywhere. So, I decide to look up where to buy blades for these. I’m directed to Sally’s, but they were out of them. Great. I guess I get to return it. But hang on!! I didn’t know that you can’t print out and package a return for them to pick up, YOU have to play delivery person! YAY! Just what I wanted-a complete fiasco made out of a stupid razor. So, now, tomorrow I get to drive to the UPS store and return, what has now become, an albatross around my neck. Needless public trips during Covid; which is EXACTLY why I’ve been ordering things! I also left a bad review, which I updated today, and noticed my bad review hadn’t been posted, and the site refuses to post my update. I hope I get my refund, and I hope my bad review of this razor, doesn’t negatively affect the other order I placed lastnight; I have left several 5 star reviews of other items I’ve been happy with. But most of all, I wish a legitimate company didn’t make me feel like they’re going to spit in my food, because I was honest enough to leave a valid review of my experience. Amazon may say they care, but their actions show us a different story.

I chatted customer service thinking maybe it was another glitch, since the last day of the return window and the last day to ship are cutting it close but are still within the window. This time customer service was terrible. Not only were the reps unfriendly, but they also kept stating the items needed to arrive at Amazon return center by that date. It doesn’t say that anywhere in the “free returns” policy or in the return label, it just says must be dropped off at ups by x date (which I did). The customer has no control over how long it takes for an item to get from the UPS store to the Amazon return center, but ok if that’s now the Amazon policy then fine just state it clearly when the order is placed and when the items are shipped back so the customer knows what to expect (I still don’t think this is the policy, I think it’s the date to have the item scanned at UPS, but the customer service rep was adamant that the ship by date was the date the item must arrive at Amazon return center - so maybe it truly has changed). Since the customer service rep was certain the ship by date for a return is when it must arrive at the Amazon return center and that’s why I was being changed a restocking fee, I then asked if I could provide feedback and share a screenshot from the return label showing that it stated to drop off at UPS by that date, not get to Amazon by that date. The customer service rep told me there was no way to provide feedback and didn’t seem to care at all. I asked about a chat transcript, rep said no way to get a transcript. I asked the rep to stay on a minute so I could grab screenshots to save, the rep promptly closed the chat and there was no way for me to get back to the chat. By this time I had wasted over an hour going in circles with the rep so I just gave up, if there’s no survey, no other way to provide feedback, no way to get a chat transcript then it seems like Amazon clearly doesn’t care how the customer service experience went anymore. I’ve considered getting prime for years and just never decided I needed it enough. Now I’m glad that I didn’t. Amazon used to pride itself on customer service and now they don’t seem to care at all since there was no avenue to provide feedback on the customer experience anywhere accessible. Even though I don’t have prime, I’ve had an Amazon account for many years and now I’m really thinking I’ll close it. Bugs and issues in the app, with shipping, returns, products etc. inevitably do happen sometimes so having the backbone of good customer service is key to feeling like I can trust a retailer. Maybe the experience is different if you’re not prime, but you’d still think that even a non prime account with many years worth of various purchases would be a valued enough customer and apparently is not valued anymore. I’d rather deal with other businesses that have much better customer service like target for day to day and Nordstrom for fashion. Ordering clothes online is always going to be hit or miss in terms of sizing so do yourself a favor and order from somewhere else with a much better return process and customer service in place to help if/when there are issues.

review_title: Amazon’s handling of fraudulent gift card orders
review_text: On Sunday, January 13th there were several orders for gift card placed on my Amazon Prime account by an unauthorized party who accessed my Amazon account between 7 and 8 AM. By pure serendipity, I accessed my account at about 8:00 that morning and, seeing the fraudulent orders, ended up reporting them to customer service within less than an hour of their being placed.  I believe the orders were placed around 7:45 and I called around 8:00.  I reported that neither I nor anyone with legitimate access to my account placed these orders.  They are, and were reported to Amazon as, fraudulent orders.When reported, Amazon's customer service representative told me they would take actions to invalidate these orders and recommended that I notify my credit card company that the orders were fraudulent.I did as recommended, however, roughly 10 days later Amazon locked my account and began sending me requests for an alternate credit card to which they could charge the gift cards.Amazon was notified of the fraudulent nature of these orders practically immediately that they happened and, I was told, intended to take appropriate actions to deal with them.  Based on their locking my account and their attempts to collect from my credit card company, I can assume that these actions were not taken.  I have spoken with Customer Service several times since this all began and, each time, have been assured that the issue would be resolved but every time, within a short time I have received another email either notifying me that Amazon was “currently working with your card issuer to resolve this dispute”, or requesting that I identify an alternate card to which the orders could be charged.Interestingly, while Customer Service seems sympathetic and helpful the responses I receive via email are from “Account Specialist, Amazon.com | Amazon Disputes Team”, are rarely signed by anyone, and seem to be worded the same depending on which of the forms I receive. Additionally, they never seem to respond directly to the emails I send in response.I've been an Amazon Prime Customer for something like 25 or 30 years (since the mid ‘90s) and have placed tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of dollars in orders over that period of time (I also use this account for purchases for my business) and yet, now, they are treating me as if I'm trying to cheat them out of a couple of hundred bucks?  Is this really how they should treat a customer who has been with them as long as I have and done as much business with them as I have?  I was taken completely by surprise, I really wouldn't have expected it of them.By the way, yesterday I discovered that they have also locked my Audible account even though, ostensibly, this is a different company. In the same vain as above I’ve been an Audible account holder for about 20 years and have something like 850 audible books in my library.  Several times I have asked Amazon to “Please” reopen my account and deal with these fraudulent orders as originally promised.  Thus far, no luck and, actually, no real responsive replies from the “Amazon Disputes Team”.

review_text: If I give zero stars I would. Today I had to contact customer service because I placed an order on a Thursday, I don’t have prime by the way, and paid for TWO DAY SHIPPING. What comes to mind when you see “Two- Day Shipping”? My thought was well let me pay $17.00 for two day because I want it to come a lot faster as a special event was coming up and I made a last ditch effort to get a gift. Yes I know it’s my fault for being so late for a gift but I trusted amazon for being a very fast delivery company, the convenience is astronomical. Order one thing today and get it by the next. Seems good right? Well I paid for two day shipping and expected it (as in the name) for it to be shipped out the same day and be received two days AFTER the order was placed. This has been the case countless times when I used amazon in the past. That’s why I choose amazon. So this time it wasn’t the case, my item shipped out three days after the order was placed and I called with my confused self and I got nothing but attitude and defensive wording and blame game. I told them that Two Day Shipping is different from Two Day Delivery. Two Day Delivery is when you order something and regardless of when you order it, it will be delivered within two days of whenever the order being placed. Two day shipping is more of it will shipped two day when you place the order. I mean it’s all about convenience with amazon so if you can kind of have a play on words with customers but still not break the “contract” they still win because they keep your money based of your assumptions. Like anyone, I would have assumed that when I’m trying to buy something under pressure or time constraint and I see “if you pay $17.00 extra, you can get Two Day Shipping”. My thought “oh that’s convenient cause I need it pretty much now” but that wasn’t the case. I just wish it was more apparent as to what they are saying right there when you purchase a different shipping method rather then having you just assume something based off the wording. They need better customer service as well.

I am an individual who has been selling products on Amazon for over ten years. I order products through a drop ship wholesaler who represents hundreds of manufacturers and over 13,000 products. Our wholesale outlet is one of the most respected in the country and purchases only from verified trademark holders for redistribution. Because of the numbers involved, the manufacturers might not know my name. However, I have an account in good standing with the wholesaler. I list my products on Amazon by means of a data feed directly from the wholesaler. Occasionally a manufacturer/trademark holder may grow concerned about counterfeit products offered on Amazon and submit blanket complaints about every retailer they see on Amazon whose name they do not recognize. This happened to me. When this happens I immediately contact the wholesaler to ask for a letter of verification and an introduction to the manufacturer/trademark holders as proof that I sell products sourced only from the trademark holder - not counterfeits. I also request and receive letters of verification from the manufacturer/trademark holder. At Amazon's request I also submitted invoices from the wholesaler to show that I purchase products from the legitimate source. These letters and invoice are attached as Exhibits to this complaint. Once these documents have been submitted Amazon stopped communicating with me. All I received were automated e-mails stating that I need to submit the documents I already submitted. Using automation Amazon repeats the same complaint and document request over and over ignoring the documentation sent to them. After several automated e-mails, Amazon stopped replying altogether. After several weeks of sending automated e-mails Amazon suspended my account and held the funds for the sales I had already completed. The unpaid balance due to me is $312.68. When I requested the release of the funds, Amazon sent one automated e-mail saying I could expect a response in 7 days. I contacted them again after 14 days and received an automated response saying Amazon will not release the funds, they will not provide the reason and will no longer communicate with me. The customer paid me, not Amazon,for the merchandise I delivered. This money does not belong to Amazon. The maneuver of not transmitting to me the proceeds of my sales does not seem to be even legal. The use of robot e-mail replies on Amazon's part hints to my mind at fraudulent intent.Additional Information: I believe this process of (1) Accusing a seller of wrongdoing (2) Ignoring a seller's defense (3) Holding the seller's balance due presumably for be kept as Amazon's personal business property - this process is a generalized fraudulent scheme. The basis for my belief is the number of complaints by sellers on Amazon who has voiced the same complaint.

review_text: Placed an order to upgrade a PC on Monday 9/3 at 07:45 promised delivery date is Tuesday 9/4 before 20:00.Fast forward to Tuesday 9/4 at 04:46 I get an email that Amazon believes my account has been compromised, SO, my account is disabled, all changes to the account have been reversed, all orders CANCELLED.How they came to this decision that the account was compromised, is beyond me.  I did change to a new credit card, and changed my phone number from my VOIP phone to my cell.  Question, if you believe that my account is compromised, why not contact me?  Ask first, just do not take unilateral action.In the meantime they had not even sent a pre-authorization to my bank, I called my bank to see if the block was on their end.  IT WAS NOT.Decided to try again, placed the same order at 08:15 Tuesday, while on the phone with their alleged Customer Service.  Order is now set to arrive Thursday prior to 20:00, not happy at all about this, but OK.Fast forward to 15:40 I have noted my bank has not been pinged for the cost of the parts.  Again call alleged Customer Service, they say there is no problem, the parts are guaranteed to arrive Thursday.  Again not happy, but OK.at 16:27 I receive the following Email:I understand your concern, as well as your desire to get this matter resolved quickly. To help prevent unauthorized charges to your credit card, certain orders must go through a manual review process that takes 1-2 business days.I'm sorry, but there is no way to speed up this process. We greatly appreciate your patience with our security measures.Once we've completed our review process and received authorization from your bank to proceed with the charge, we'll begin processing your order.We hope to see you again soon.We'd appreciate your feedback. Please use the buttons below to vote about your experience today.Best regards,Nancy O.Amazon.com Now we are 2 days into this debacle, and NOTHING has been accomplished, other then to anger me. So it seems it will be another day AT LEAST before Amazon gets around to decide if they want my money. This is after 3  phone calls, multiple emails.  I want to know how they are going to VERIFY me, are they going to visit me at home or at work in person?    And really NO WAY TO SPEED UP THE PROCESS?  Sounds like a delaying tactic to me.  Though they insist that the parts will arrive arrive Thursday 9/6.  Tell me, has Amazon mastered time travel, that is the only way to get things not shipped on time delivered on time.Fast forward to 08:30 Wednesday 9/5  bank has still not been contacted about the amount or any inquiry made about my account.  Call Alleged Customer Service again, told to be patient.  all is well parts will arrive on time.  09:00 Wednesday 9/5 decide I have had enough of Amazon and their alleged Security Policy, Cancelled order, went to another vendor, paid $10 more for the parts, and an extra $35.00 for next day shipping. Once again I had to contact customer service, I got a refund and I asked them close the account.It is easier to get a loan in the bank than it is to open a seller account on Amazon.
